- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) and forecast is below recent high, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is above recent low, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 3rd–5th day after a sentiment spike — add 1–2% buffer to forecast for such periods.  
- Model overestimates mean reversion in early horizon (1–3 days) — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is zero for 3+ consecutive days, model should not assume trend continuation — forecast should revert to 30-day moving average.  
- Overshoots after sharp upward sentiment moves (e.g., >0.67) are common — cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent peak for next 3 days.  
- Model often misses late-period (last 5–7 days) sentiment-driven corrections — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment turns negative after peak.
